results.evidence: Published car-to-car times for this route spread from under 7 hours to about 10.5 hours depending on pace: one party reports under 7 hours, another about 8.5 hours (4.75 h up), another 5.4 h up and 4.9 h down (10.3 h), another ~2 h to the basin plus 3 h to the summit. The ascent of ~5 hours is well agreed, but no two sources agree on a descent time or single car-to-car figure; settling it needs a chosen pace convention (e.g. restate timing/totalNote as a 7-10.5 h range, or align the schedule's summit time and descent to 9 h).

results.correct_value: Climbable Jun-Sep (June is an early-season option with lots of snow); most reliable mid-July through September
results.evidence: The peak's standard description gives June through September as the climbing window depending on snow, and a documented ascent was made on June 27; other accounts note an axe is needed earlier in the season and rock-only conditions by late September. So Jun-Sep is correct as the window, but June is snowy shoulder season rather than 'not the intended season', and 'best conditions June-September' overstates June.

results.correct_value: An exposed class 3 scramble (one short class 3.5 slot) on mostly solid rock
results.evidence: One report calls the finish a delightful Class 3 scramble on solid rock above a V-shaped Class 3.5 slot; another describes class 3 with some exposure on solid rock via easy gully systems, and warns harder-than-class-3 ground means you are off route; a third calls the crux groove the most solid rock of the day at Class 3. None describes a long, loose class 3-4 chimney.

results.fact: Gold Run Pass vs the Tomyhoi Lake fork
results.correct_value: The 1.5-mile pin is the Yellow Aster Butte / Tomyhoi Lake trail junction, below Gold Run Pass; the route does not cross the pass
results.evidence: The land manager's trail page puts the junction with Yellow Aster Butte Trail 686.1 about 1.5 miles from the trailhead, with the Tomyhoi Lake trail continuing upward through meadow to Gold Run Pass; a trail guide adds the pass is about another half mile on, ~1,800 ft above the trailhead. The pin's 5,427 ft is the pass's height, not the junction's, and the junction's own height is unsourced, so it is set to unknown.

results.evidence: Round-trip gain figures for this route disagree: 5,600 ft (one detailed report), 5,000 ft (a club route page, and 5,000+ elsewhere), 5,400 ft, and 4,800 ft. The 5,000 figure has two loosely agreeing sources but one gives an impossible 5-mile distance, so neither 5,000 nor 5,600 is settled; a measured GPS track of this route would settle it.
